items.title: cactus-compute/needle
items.contentSnippet:
14MB foundation model for tiny devices; phones, wearables, smart home, and robots.


 
Needle 2
 
Needle 2 is an open 45M-parameter model for tool calling, device use and structured extraction. The whole model is a single 14MB binary that runs a full session in about 28MB of RAM. It is built on our Simple Attention Network findings, compressed to CQ2-bit with Cactus Quants, and baked into its own engine. items.title: Show HN: Ask questions about the Swiss train timetable
items.contentSnippet:
I use the SBB website and app every day to find my Swiss train journeys, but even with the touch tiles I find it cumbersome to use, especially for extra filters like avoiding bus or finding trains with space for bicycles.
So I built https://fragplan.ch/ to describe a train journey in natural language, and translate it into an SBB timetable request. I'm especially happy about the many settings one can make on SBB.

items.title: Show HN: Meridian, a local-first journal that drafts project updates
items.contentSnippet:
Meridian is an open-source, local-first work journal for developers. It reconstructs your day from on-screen activity, creates daily summaries and standups, tracks where your time went, and drafts project ticket updates for review. Your activity is stored in an encrypted database on your machine, and Meridian is available under the MIT License.

items.title: An eval harness found what qualitative review couldn't: AI models are most confident when wrong
items.contentSnippet:
There is a step in the development process for large language model (LLM)-assisted tooling that most teams skip because it's tedious, time-consuming, and doesn't produce results visible to end users: Verifying that what the model is saying is actually correct.
